summary: Carpentero presents the evolution of LLM attacks from 2023 prompt injection to today's multi-vector threat landscape, now the baseline in production systems. Six attack vectors are detailed. Direct injection exploits the lack of native separation between system controls and user data, illustrated by the Sydney/Bing Chat case exfiltrating 40+ confidential rules. Indirect injection places malicious instructions in external content; a March 2025 case showed AI advertising review systems being overruled by the data they evaluate. The LLM internals vector uses gibberish suffix tokens optimized via greedy coordinate gradient search, transferring to black-box models due to geometrically similar refusal boundaries. RAG poisoning requires only 5 chunks in an 8-million-document database. MCP exploits leverage asymmetry between user-visible summaries and full LLM-read descriptions for credential exfiltration. Agentic attacks achieve remote code execution, including a supply chain attack affecting 4,000-5,000 developers via a malicious NPM package installed through a GitHub issue prompt injection. Carpentero frames the Zero Trust Gap: LLMs have no native separation of concerns, alignment is probabilistic not hard constraint, and human reviewers face the iceberg effect. The solution is fine-tuning ModernBERT as a safety discriminator using the Inject Guard dataset of 75,000 labeled examples from 20 sources. ModernBERT's architectural innovations enable this: alternating attention combines two local layers (128-token sliding window) with every third global layer (8192 tokens), matching attack patterns. Unpadding and sequence packing eliminate up to 50% wasted computation. The deep-narrow architecture (22 layers/768 hidden dims in base, 28/1024 in large) refines the CLS token through multiple semantic abstraction levels, with dimensions aligned to tensor operations as multiples of 64. Rotary positional encoding (RoPE) rotates query and key projections by relative position angle instead of adding position vectors, avoiding semantic entanglement and enabling continuous context windows limited only by geometry, with adjusted rotation speeds for local versus global attention to prevent full-cycle aliasing. FlashAttention processes sequences in blocks within ultra-fast on-chip GPU memory (30+ TB/s) rather than materializing the full attention matrix, avoiding the bottleneck of off-chip memory transfers. The fine-tuning pipeline uses Hugging Face Datasets for train/test splits, byte-pair encoding tokenization with CLS and SEP special tokens, dynamic padding, a classification head on the CLS token output, brain floating point format (40% memory reduction enabling batch size 64), and the Adam optimizer. The large model achieves ~85% accuracy at 35ms per classification on unseen benchmark data. A live demo tests prompts from the research cases: the Sydney prompt injection and impersonation attempts are classified as unsafe, the Wikipedia malicious redirect is detected, the AI advertising review manipulation is classified as unsafe, a gibberish suffix internals attack is classified as unsafe, and the MCP credential exfiltration exploit exploiting user-model asymmetry is also classified as unsafe. Carpentero emphasizes this is a baseline, not a gold standard, and encourages everyone to build defensive layers with commodity hardware and collaboratively develop safer AI systems.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Threat Landscape
sections.summary: Carpentero frames the evolution of LLM attacks from 2023 prompt injection to today's sophisticated, multi-vector threat landscape, now the baseline rather than the exception. Introduces the plan to build a low-latency, self-hosted defensive layer by fine-tuning ModernBERT, previewing architectural components like alternating attention, RoPE, and FlashAttention.

sections.title: Prompt Vector (Direct Injection)
sections.summary: Defines direct injection as crafted user input overriding system controls. Details the Sydney/Bing Chat case where a Stanford student used natural language to exfiltrate the system prompt, codename, and 40+ confidential rules. Explains the root cause: LLMs concatenate system and user prompts into one document with no native separation of concerns.

sections.title: Context Vector (Indirect Injection)
sections.summary: Describes indirect injection where malicious instructions are placed in external content. Covers a Wikipedia/Albert Einstein POC redirecting to malware, and a real March 2025 case where websites embed prompts manipulating AI advertising review systems into approving non-compliant content.

sections.title: LLM Internals Vector
sections.summary: Explains attacks exploiting model mathematics via gibberish suffix tokens that shift next-token probability distributions past refusal boundaries. Details greedy coordinate gradient optimization and the critical finding that these attacks transfer to black-box models due to geometrically similar refusal boundaries from similar training.

sections.title: RAG Vector
sections.summary: Presents poisoned RAG findings: only 5 poisoned chunks in an 8-million-document database suffice when retrieval and generation conditions are met. The attack surface is growing larger and more mutable.

sections.title: MCP Vector
sections.summary: Describes MCP exploits leveraging asymmetry between simplified tool summaries shown to users and full descriptions read by LLMs. Hidden instructions can exfiltrate private keys and credentials as hidden parameters.

sections.title: Agentic Vector
sections.summary: Covers attacks targeting actions of compromised LLMs in autonomous environments. A researcher created an HTML page tricking an agent into downloading and executing a file. Mentions a February 2025 supply chain attack affecting 4,000-5,000 developers via a malicious NPM package installed through a GitHub issue prompt injection.

sections.title: Zero Trust Gap and Consequences
sections.summary: Frames the Zero Trust Gap: LLMs lack native separation of concerns between system controls and data, violating the zero trust principle. Model alignment is probabilistic, not a hard constraint. Human reviewers face the iceberg effect. Consequences span three dimensions: what is told, what is done, and what is believed. Minimum production safety checks should cover user inputs and model responses, ideally also retrieval, MCPs, context memory, and agentic plans.

sections.title: Encoder Models as Safety Discriminators
sections.summary: Explains why encoder models suit AI safety checks: safety discrimination is a classification problem. Bidirectional attention lets them see all tokens in one forward pass, producing a dense CLS token representation for a classification head. Fine-tuned classification takes 35ms baseline. LLM-as-a-Judge compounds into seconds of latency. Encoder models can be retrained within hours and self-hosted for privacy.

sections.title: ModernBERT Architecture: Alternating Attention
sections.summary: Details alternating attention: two local attention layers with a 128-token sliding window followed by every third layer as global attention with 8192 tokens. This matches attack patterns—gibberish suffixes and GitHub title injections are locally concentrated, while creative writing, MCP descriptions, and agentic plans need long context. Traditional global attention has quadratic complexity, fine for 512 tokens but not scalable.

sections.title: ModernBERT Architecture: Unpadding and Sequence Packing
sections.summary: Explains unpadding and sequence packing. Traditional padding wastes up to 50% computation on meaningless tokens. ModernBERT removes padding before the embedding layer and concatenates semantic tokens until filling the 8192-token context, processing all sequences in a single forward pass with attention masking.

sections.title: ModernBERT Architecture: Deep and Narrow Design
sections.summary: Describes ModernBERT's deep-narrow architecture: 22 layers/768 hidden dims (base), 28 layers/1024 (large), grid-searched for task performance and inference speed. More layers refine the CLS token through multiple semantic abstraction levels. Narrow configuration and FlashAttention compensate for slower processing from more layers.

sections.title: ModernBERT Architecture: Implementation Choices and RoPE
sections.summary: Covers remaining implementation choices: dimensions aligned to tensor operations as multiples of 64, gate activation function for suppressing or amplifying information, bias terms disabled except in final decoder for more useful parameter capacity, and normalization after embedding for training stability. Details rotary positional encoding (RoPE): instead of adding position vectors (which entangle position with token semantics and limit context to training size), RoPE rotates query and key projections by relative position angle. Attention scores encode token distance via rotation geometry, enabling continuous context windows limited only by geometry. ModernBERT adjusts rotation steps—faster for local attention, slower for global—to prevent full-cycle aliasing where distant tokens appear close.

sections.title: ModernBERT Architecture: FlashAttention
sections.summary: Explains FlashAttention's insight from GPU memory hierarchy: on-chip memory is ultra-fast (30+ TB/s) while off-chip is ~10x slower. The bottleneck is memory transfers, not floating point operations. FlashAttention avoids materializing the full attention matrix by processing sequences in blocks, computing partial attention scores in on-chip memory and accumulating results. This is a main contributor to the 35ms inference latency. Summarizes all architectural improvements enabling the fine-tuning of a low-latency self-hosted defensive layer.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning Pipeline and Dataset
sections.summary: Introduces the Inject Guard dataset of 75,000 labeled examples from 20 sources for fine-tuning. Recommends starting with the base version (~150M parameters) to test the pipeline, then switching to large for ~6 point accuracy improvement. Covers dataset preparation with Hugging Face Datasets for train/test splits, tokenization with byte-pair encoding (~50,000 word vocabulary), CLS and SEP special tokens, dynamic padding for variable-length batches, and the classification head on the CLS token output with option for mean pooling on long sequences.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning Optimization and Results
sections.summary: Details hyperparameters: brain floating point format reduces training memory by ~40% enabling batch size 64, Adam optimizer, and FlashAttention for GPU inference. The fine-tuned large model achieves almost 85% accuracy on unseen benchmark data at 35ms per classification. References technical documentation and GitHub repo.

sections.title: Live Demo: Attack Prompts Tested Against Fine-Tuned Model
sections.summary: Demonstrates the fine-tuned model classifying real attack prompts from the research cases. The Sydney/Bing Chat prompt injection and impersonation attempt are classified as unsafe. The Wikipedia malicious redirect is detected. The AI advertising review manipulation prompt is classified as unsafe. A gibberish suffix internals attack appending nonsensical tokens to a harmful query is classified as unsafe. The MCP credential exfiltration exploit leveraging asymmetry between user-visible summaries and full LLM-read descriptions is also classified as unsafe. Carpentero emphasizes this is a baseline, not a gold standard for safety, and encourages everyone to build defensive layers with commodity hardware and collaboratively develop safer AI systems.
